Subject: SOC 2: request for VM evidence + canary patch plan

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for taking this. FinVantage's SOC 2 auditor is asking us to produce a short packet that shows (1) scan cadence for infrastructure and images, (2) SLA commitments for CVE remediation by severity, and (3) evidence of a canary/rollout plan used for high-risk patches.

Could you send:
- Your current scan cadence (what runs daily/weekly/monthly and what is authenticated vs unauthenticated)
- The SLA table you apply to CVE severities (we need exact time windows from detection/triage to remediation)
- A short canary plan or playbook excerpt (example steps and rollback criteria) and any recent example where a canary rollout was used
- Latest consolidated scan report (PDF) covering host and container scans

Auditor would prefer a single folder (Drive link) and a short attestation letter stating Redwood will meet the stated SLAs for SOC 2 compliance. Do you already have a stock attestation we can upload?

Goal: get this to the auditor by end of week. Let me know if any of this requires a legal or procurement review (procurement@finvantage.com is on standby).

Best,
Lisa Murray
Head of Security, FinVantage

Hi Lisa —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached the PDF and a canary plan workbook for your auditor. See attachments: redwood_weekly_scan_20260220.pdf, canary_patch_plan_20260224.xlsx, and a short evidence index document.

Scan cadence (summary):
- Daily: lightweight container image SBOM & SCA checks (unauthenticated), daily build-time SCA alerts integrated into CI pipelines.
- Weekly: authenticated host and container full vulnerability scan (Friday 02:00 UTC), includes NVD/CVSS mapping and custom fingerprinting for our runtime infra.
- Monthly: third-party dependency deep-scan (license + supply-chain checks) and manual review of any long-lived exceptions.
- On-demand: rapid hotpatch scan triggered immediately after a critical/zero-day advisory is published; we also run targeted scans for affected images/services.

CVE remediation SLAs (applies from detection/triage):
- Critical (RCE/elevation/service-impact): 48 hours to remediation or documented mitigations + canary rollout planned within 48 hours.
- High (exploit likely, medium impact): 7 days to remediation or scheduled mitigation with tracking.
- Medium: 30 days to remediation or scheduled backlog with compensating controls.
- Low: handled in regular maintenance windows (documented, typically 90 days).

Canary & rollback summary (attached workbook has step-by-step):
- Canary staging: deploy to a 10% subset of hosts/replicas in the same AZ, monitor health & error rates for minimum 2-hour observation window.
- Telemetry: latency, error-rate, CPU/memory, custom anomaly detectors (alerts at 2x baseline).
- Rollback criteria: >=3% sustained error-rate increase over baseline OR any data-integrity exception; automated rollback if critical failures observed.
- Post-canary: 24-hour broader staging at 50% then full rollout.

Attestation: we maintain a templated attestation for SOC 2 VM evidence. Please find a short draft attestation in the Drive link below; we can sign and DocuSign if you need.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FvFinVantageEvidence

CC'ing Monica and Karthik — Monica is our VM owner for triage cadence; Karthik is tracking remediation owners for infra components. If you need a signed letter, Monica will coordinate.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_weekly_scan_20260220.pdf (report); canary_patch_plan_20260224.xlsx (spreadsheet); evidence_index.md (doc)

Hi Naomi —

Quick follow-up from the auditor's review of the materials you uploaded: the auditor would like two clarifications before proceeding with evidence acceptance:
1) For a small sample of outstanding CVEs, please list the remediation owner (team or person) and the planned remediation date. We only need 3–5 sample items.
2) On the canary plan, the auditor asks for one short real-world example (last 12 months) where a canary detected an issue and led to rollback — a brief timeline is sufficient (date, service, observed symptom, action taken).

Also confirm whether Redwood uses an automated rollback mechanism or a manual intervention for initial canary failure.

Please upload the small CSV or a short doc to the Drive folder and reply so we can close this control.

Thanks,
SIG Audit Team
